implemented: production starts the adjacent notification-area-host outside the GPUI process on the first snapshot request
the client uses bounded newline-framed JSON over redirected pipes and terminates the child on write, parse, EOF, or timeout failure
the taskbar polls a generation-bound full snapshot twice per second and restarts the host on a later poll after failure
host failure clears stale icons while leaving Start, tasks, clock, and independent status providers alive
equal snapshots do not trigger redundant taskbar reconciliation
visible and overflow placement is rendered from NotificationAreaModel without synthetic registrations
overflow invocation focuses the first hidden icon and Escape/dismiss state stays inside the owned model
registered icons expose tooltip text, button roles, keyboard focus, activation, and context pointer routes
activation and context events are timestamped, bounded, admitted only for a registered icon, and can be drained only by the owning client
event and snapshot host calls are bounded to 100 milliseconds in the production taskbar path
validated owned RGBA icon payloads are converted to GPUI render images for both visible and overflow placements; a neutral marker is used only when the client supplied no bitmap
deliberately_not_claimed: legacy Shell_NotifyIcon/WM_COPYDATA compatibility; Windows exposes no documented notification-area hosting API and the design forbids undocumented toolbar emulation, so the current isolated host accepts the published SuperDesktop notification protocol
physical p95 event latency evidence; this remains an external evidence-machine gate
